clue.text: Inspect each benefit

blocks.note: per means each, as in ten pounds per head
use is benefit or advantage, as in what's the use

explanation.surface: An auditor checking every perk or payment someone receives.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse something is to read or examine it carefully, a close synonym of looking it over.

clue.text: Bang on about recipes

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved here and there, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: all seven letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone droning on about recipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang on about' reads as talk tediously about; the definition is just 'Bang on', meaning exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is informal British for spot on or exact, which is what precise means.

clue.text: Leave an impression after really top gag

indicators.note: after puts the first piece second, placed behind the single letter
the top of a down entry's word is its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
to etch is to cut a lasting mark or impression into a surface

explanation.surface: A comedian whose really excellent joke makes a lasting impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke; here it is the verb, to heave as if about to vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit, the same reflex as gagging.

clue.text: Agent is one out for the count

blocks.note: first meaning: a spy planted to lie dormant until called on
second meaning: someone fast asleep, out cold like a knocked-down boxer

explanation.surface: A secret agent has been knocked out in the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormant spy is called by this name, and so is anyone deeply asleep.

clue.text: Read erratically, following quiet joint

indicators.note: something done erratically is done without fixed order, so the letters come out jumbled
coming after another word, so the jumbled part is placed second in the build

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
the four letters of the word jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling over their reading after a quiet smoke of a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a cannabis cigarette in the surface; here it is the adjective, as in a joint account.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held jointly is owned or used in common by several people, the adjectival sense of joint.

clue.text: Harry initially going astray for swimmer

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: opening letter of the name
erring means straying from the right path

explanation.surface: Harry gets lost on his way to meet a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a small silvery sea fish, and fish are swimmers in crossword language.

clue.text: Not serving rice, given stew

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture cooked together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook refusing to serve rice because a stew has been dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not serving' looks like a waiter refusing food; it is tennis, where the player not serving is receiving.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the player facing the server is said to be receiving, returning the ball.

clue.text: Nearly set aside dodgy complaint

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
something dodgy is unreliable and out of true, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the word without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone almost dismisses a suspicious grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' reads as one phrase; only 'set' is shortened, then joined to 'aside' and the seven letters jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment, so it can mean a disease.

clue.text: Have enough money for a French car

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for French
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one can pay for a French-made car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A French car' suggests a Peugeot or Renault; the car is a Ford, with French giving only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have sufficient funds to pay for it.

clue.text: 'Car of sweetheart polluted' (statement about climate change)

indicators.note: something polluted has been spoilt and mixed with other matter, so these letters are thoroughly scrambled

blocks.note: the fifteen letters of the quoted phrase, all used

explanation.surface: A quoted lament about a lover's car spewing fumes, offered as a comment on global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface frames the brackets as an environmental aside; read loosely, a forecast does announce how the climate, the weather, is about to change.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast is a broadcast prediction telling viewers how conditions outdoors will shift over coming days.

clue.text: Repeat dance for man on board

blocks.note: bis is a musical direction meaning play it again, twice
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A call for an encore at a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; the board is a chessboard, and the man a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the chess pieces, and chess pieces are traditionally called men.

clue.text: First exam covers writer with spirit

indicators.note: a thing that covers others sits around them, so this word wraps the following pieces

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A first test in which the candidate writes about a spirited character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' as I is a crossword convention: the setter speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Original can mean the earliest or first version of something, before any copies were made.

clue.text: Considered Matilda as terribly rude

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly, with the letters thrown out of their order

blocks.note: Matilda is this puzzle's setter, so her name stands for me
taken as written
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone has judged the setter to be very rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Matilda is the setter's pseudonym, so the name gives ME, just as 'setter' often does.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is a considered one, carefully weighed rather than hasty.

clue.text: Protected Theresa deal, but not as planned

indicators.note: but not as asks for every copy of the letter A to be taken out, reading the word as plural A's
planned means arranged, so the surviving letters are set out in a fresh order

blocks.note: the name and the noun taken as written

explanation.surface: A Brexit agreement shielded from criticism, though it did not go as Theresa May intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not as planned' looks like one phrase; 'as' is read as the plural of the letter A, so both A's go before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered means shielded or protected from harm, weather or hardship.

clue.text: Escorts for girls

blocks.note: first meaning: leads or shows the way, as a verb
second meaning: members of the Girl ..., the youth movement for girls

explanation.surface: Chaperones hired to accompany young women.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for leading people somewhere and the name for members of a uniformed girls' organisation.

clue.text: Be there when the news is read at last

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so only the closing letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: News at Ten is a long-running evening bulletin on British TV, so the news is on at ten
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets around to listening to the news being read.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is ITV's evening news programme in Britain, which supplies the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, so it fits being there.

clue.text: Police car returns holding up houses

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters inside it, spanning the word breaks
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A police car comes back and is stuck in traffic outside a row of homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like the reversal signal; it is part of the hiding phrase, and the turnaround comes from 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a common British street form.

clue.text: Professionals court indoors

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, the short abbreviation going within the word that follows

blocks.note: split as in plus doors; the second half is the outer word
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Lawyers or other experts woo someone inside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indoors' reads as one word; split it into the container signal and the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors are qualified medical practitioners, one example of the learned professions.

clue.text: Fix mood having drunk a barrel

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker, so these letters take the next ones into their middle

blocks.note: taken as written
a keg is a small barrel

explanation.surface: Someone cheers themself up by downing an entire barrel of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to repair or put right damage, a phrasal synonym of fix.

clue.text: Gosh, takes dole back in part?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read right to left
something that takes another holds it, so the exclamation goes around the other piece

blocks.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh
taken as written

explanation.surface: Surprise that someone has taken their unemployment benefit back in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit. 'Part' looks like a portion; it is a musical part, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the melody is the tune line, one of the parts a singer or player performs.

clue.text: Secured some junk, not Ted's

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone tied up a few items of rubbish that turn out not to be Ted's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something knotted has been tied fast with a knot, so it is fastened or made secure.

clue.text: My friend's used kidney, say

blocks.note: used things are second-hand or old
the kidney is one type of bean, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: A grim confession that a friend has a transplanted kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: Old bean is a dated, jolly British form of address meaning old chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a chummy upper-class British way of addressing a pal, like old fellow.

clue.text: Major's really sick

blocks.note: first meaning: of great importance, crucial
second meaning: gravely ill, as a hospital might describe a patient's condition

explanation.surface: An army major is seriously unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as an officer's rank; here it is the adjective meaning important.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a decisive, important matter and a patient in danger of dying.

clue.text: Where fielders may be in a position to play

blocks.note: first meaning: on the leg side of a cricket pitch
second meaning: not offside in football or rugby, so legally able to play the ball

explanation.surface: Describing a cricket team's placing of fielders ready for the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a half of the cricket field and, in football, a player legally positioned to receive the ball.

clue.text: Labours small records

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
logs are written records, as kept by a ship

explanation.surface: Minor files kept by a political party, Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To slog is to toil hard and persistently, so it is a synonym of labouring.

clue.text: Hotel with cooler bathroom product

blocks.note: Hotel is the radio alphabet word for H
an air conditioner is a machine that cools a room

explanation.surface: A hotel boasting air-cooled rooms and toiletries in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair conditioner is a cream applied after shampoo in the shower, a typical toiletry.

clue.text: First of children to turn 13 (not her)

indicators.note: not her asks for those three letters to be removed from the word referred to
to turn means to be turned around and rearranged, so what remains is reordered

blocks.note: the answer to clue 13 in this grid, the down entry

explanation.surface: The firstborn child is about to turn thirteen, and the bracket points out it is a boy, not a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' looks like an age but refers to 13-down; take H, E, R out of that answer and rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the one born first in a family.

clue.text: Likely to happen for strange boy

blocks.note: odd means strange
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A prediction about a peculiar child.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is a betting term for a favourite expected to win, so it means probable.
